title: Replacement Property Identification
name: Replacement Property Identification
metaTitle: Replacement Property Identification in Phoenix, AZ
metaDescription: Building and filing your written identification list for a Phoenix 1031 exchange, matched to real candidate properties before the 45-day clock starts.

sections.html: Identification is a paperwork deadline with a real property search behind it. We build the candidate list and the written notice together so day forty-five doesn't sneak up on you with nothing solid on it.

sections.heading: What the Written Identification Actually Requires
sections.html: Your qualified intermediary needs an unambiguous description of each candidate property, generally the street address or legal description, delivered in writing before midnight on day forty-five after your relinquished property closes. A verbal mention to your QI or a text message with a vague description is not enough. We draft the notice language directly with your QI so the description standard is met the first time.

sections.heading: Matching Candidates to a Phoenix Market That Moves Fast
sections.html: Industrial along the West Valley growth corridor, multifamily in the newer submarkets, and net lease retail pads all move on different timelines. We build your candidate list from properties that are actually available and priced, not properties that were on the market two months ago and already gone. That means we're pulling live listings and off-market leads right up until you file.

sections.heading: How We Structure a Candidate List
sections.html:
Every identification list we help build follows the same discipline:

  • Confirm which identification rule your QI is applying to the exchange
  • Rank candidates by how close they are to actually closable
  • Keep at least one backup candidate in case the top choice falls through
  • Verify legal description or address accuracy before it goes to the QI
  • Confirm the notice is delivered and acknowledged in writing before day forty-five

That backup candidate has saved more than one exchange when a top-choice deal died in diligence after day forty-five had already passed.

sections.heading: The Rule Choice Behind the List
sections.html: Investors generally choose among identifying up to three properties regardless of value, or a longer list under the two-hundred-percent rule, or an even longer list under the ninety-five-percent rule if enough of it eventually closes. Which rule applies to your exchange is a decision for you, your qualified intermediary, and your tax advisor. We build the candidate list to fit whichever rule you've chosen, not the other way around.

sections.heading: Why We Start Before Your Sale Closes
sections.html: The forty-five days start running the day your relinquished property closes, and Phoenix diligence timelines don't pause for that clock. We start building your candidate list while your sale is still under contract so you're identifying vetted properties on day one of the window instead of day thirty.

sections.heading: What a Real Phoenix Identification List Looks Like
sections.html:
On a recent exchange out of a sold retail property, the investor's final list carried a West Valley industrial building as the primary candidate, a similarly sized net lease pad on Bell Road as a close backup, and a small multifamily property in Mesa as a third option in case financing on the first two didn't come together in time. That third slot never got used, the primary candidate closed, but having it in writing meant the investor wasn't exposed if the industrial deal had fallen apart during diligence.

That's the pattern we build toward on most Phoenix identification lists: one strong primary candidate, one close backup in the same asset class, and a genuine third option rather than a placeholder property nobody intends to buy.

sections.heading: Keeping the QI in the Loop as the List Changes
sections.html: Candidate lists shift right up until the deadline as properties go under contract to other buyers or new listings surface. We keep your qualified intermediary updated on the working list throughout the window, all the way through the final version on day forty-five, so there's no confusion about which draft is the one that actually gets filed.

sections.heading: What Happens After You File
sections.html: Once the written identification is delivered and acknowledged, your focus shifts to closing on whichever candidate you're moving forward with before the one-hundred-eighty-day deadline. We stay involved through that stretch too, since financing, inspection, and title work on a Phoenix property can still surface issues that need a quick decision rather than a slow one.

sections.heading: A Note on Off-Market Candidates
sections.html: Some of the strongest Phoenix candidates never hit public listing sites, especially in tight submarkets where sellers work directly with brokers they already know. We keep relationships across the metro so your candidate list includes properties you'd otherwise never see, well beyond whatever happens to be posted publicly during your search window.

faqs.q: What counts as a valid written identification for a 1031 exchange?
faqs.a: Generally a street address or legal description delivered in writing to your qualified intermediary before the forty-five-day deadline. A verbal mention or vague description doesn't meet the standard, so we draft the notice language directly with your QI.

faqs.q: Can I change my identified properties after I submit the list?
faqs.a: Once the forty-five-day window closes, the list is generally locked under the rule your qualified intermediary applied. That's why we build in a backup candidate before the deadline, not after.

faqs.q: How early should I start looking for replacement property in Phoenix?
faqs.a: Before your relinquished property closes, if possible. Phoenix inventory in growth submarkets moves fast enough that waiting until day one of the identification window can mean your best candidates are already gone.

faqs.q: Do you decide which identification rule I should use?
faqs.a: No. That's a decision for you, your qualified intermediary, and your tax advisor based on your specific exchange. We build your candidate list to match whichever rule you've chosen.

faqs.q: What happens if my top identified property falls out of escrow after day forty-five?
faqs.a: If you identified a backup candidate within the window, you may still be able to close on it. That's exactly why we always push for at least one backup on the list.
